sections.heading: When to use
sections.text: Use LCC for high-output-voltage applications where parasitic capacitance is significant. LCC uses a parallel capacitor instead of a parallel inductor (as in LLC). The parallel capacitor can absorb transformer parasitic capacitance.

sections.heading: Key difference from LLC
sections.text: LCC has a parallel capacitor Cp instead of a parallel inductor Lm. The gain characteristics are similar to LLC but the parallel resonant frequency depends on Cp. LCC is preferred when the transformer secondary has significant parasitic capacitance.

sections.heading: Controller structure
sections.text: Same as LLC: PI controller with kp in Hz/V and ki in Hz/(V*s). Operate above the series resonant frequency for ZVS. The gain curve shape depends on the ratio of Cp to Cr.
